body:
Yeah that makes sense to me.

cc @whatwg/canvas

The issue here is that there is no output bitmap for a CanvasPattern: these objects are "canvas-neutral", like `CanvasGradient` are, see the note for [addColorStop()](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-canvasgradient-addcolorstop). 

It seems that currently,

 - Safari returns `null` from `createPattern()` and thus silently ignores setting the `fillStyle` or `strokeStyle` afterward.
 - Firefox always uses the default 300x150px.
 - Chrome does use the canvas size from which the method has been called at the time it's been called.

*Personal take with no strong opinion:*  
  - Safari's behavior makes sense, even though **it's very hard to debug**. The specs do ask that if the image is not usable, it should return `null`. I think this was a mistake and throwing in such a case would have made more sense, but failing at this step *does* make sense. `createImageBitmap` is supposed to reject its promise with such an image when there is no resize option. Unlike `drawImage()`, `createPattern()` does not offer an output rect and is thus closer to `createImageBitmap` with no options. 
   - Firefox's behavior kind of makes sense to me if I try to fill the various gaps, IIRC it fits with the old way of defining the default sizing which used to fall back on a 300x150px rectangle (?). It's not so true anymore since the algo now needs a default object size.
  - Chrome's behavior is surprising to me. I would not expect the context on which `createPattern()` has been called to matter (actually I'd argue for exposing `CanvasPattern` and `CanvasGradient` constructors directly, but I digress).  Unlike `drawImage()` the "use time" is not defined here and we don't know what will be the output bitmap's size at the time of drawing. It's not uncommon to prepare the `CanvasPattern` objects once and not recreate them afterward. Having a pattern fit nicely on one frame and not matching anymore just because the user resized the screen would be very surprising and hard to notice for a dev.

> The issue here is that there is no output bitmap for a CanvasPattern: these objects are "canvas-neutral", like `CanvasGradient` are, see the note for [addColorStop()](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-canvasgradient-addcolorstop).

...

> * Chrome's behavior is surprising to me. I would not expect the context on which `createPattern()` has been called to matter (actually I'd argue for exposing `CanvasPattern` and `CanvasGradient` constructors directly, but I digress).  Unlike `drawImage()` the "use time" is not defined here and we don't know what will be the output bitmap's size at the time of drawing. It's not uncommon to prepare the `CanvasPattern` objects once and not recreate them afterward. Having a pattern fit nicely on one frame and not matching anymore just because the user resized the screen would be very surprising and hard to notice for a dev.

If I'm understanding correctly, Chrome's behavior does have the property of the pattern adjusting as the screen/canvas is resized. Say you set a scale of 0.25 using setTransform on an SVG with no intrinsic size (aka no viewbox) and use it to fill a rect covering the canvas. You will get a 4x4 grid of SVG images, regardless of the canvas dimensions.

This is the behavior suggested above and it makes sense to me. Also, for what it's worth, it matches SVG behavior where patterns are sized at use time.

Chrome uses the size of the canvas at the pattern's *creation* time, not at its use time.  
Here is a small test-case: https://jsfiddle.net/fk4ey1wm/
Note that I'm not entirely sure of my SVG equivalences in there.  
In case I got it correctly, Chrome's behavior indeed matches one of SVG's ones: when the `patternUnit` is set to `"userSpaceOnUse"`. When it's set to `"objectBoundingBox"` (the default), SVG seems to rasterize at the source's size (the `<pattern>`'s width and height)  and then scale to the target size, but crop to 300x150 with no repeat somehow.  That sounds like a quite arbitrary behavior and I'm not sure we should follow it for canvas.  
Also, `CanvasPattern` doesn't offer a mean to set the `patternUnits`, and I'm not sure what it would mean there.
I misunderstood you then. Sorry. Do we agree on the desired behavior though?
